Il y a (there is, there are)
Il s'agit de (it is a matter of, it's about)

grammar_rules.title: Meanings and nuances of the verb devoir
grammar_rules.summary: Devoir expresses obligation (must/have to), owing money/favors, probability/supposition, and should (conditionnel).
grammar_rules.explanation:
1. Obligation: 'Tu dois partir' (You must leave).
2. Owing: 'Je vous dois dix euros' (I owe you 10 euros).
3. Probability: 'Il doit être midi' (It must be noon / It probably is noon).
4. Advice / Should (in conditional): 'Vous devriez appeler' (You should call).

steps: je dois, tu dois, il doit, nous devons, vous devez, ils doivent

grammar_rules.title: Existential and temporal uses of il y a
grammar_rules.summary: Means 'there is / there are' with nouns; in negation becomes 'il n'y a pas de'; inverted 'y a-t-il?'.
grammar_rules.explanation: Il y a is invariable regardless of whether singular or plural follows: 'Il y a un livre', 'Il y a des livres'. Negative form: 'Il n'y a pas de problème'.
notes: Partitive changes to 'de' in negative: 'Il n'y a pas d'eau'.

common_mistakes.explanation: Il y a never changes to plural.

grammar_rules.title: The impersonal construction il s'agit de
grammar_rules.summary: Translates to 'it is about / it is a matter of / it concerns'. Always uses impersonal subject 'il'.
grammar_rules.explanation: 'Dans ce livre, il s'agit du président' (In this book, it's about the president). In question form: 'De quoi s'agit-il?' (What is it about?).
usage_conditions: Identifying topics, subjects of discussion, critical matters
restrictions: Never use personal subjects (ce livre s'agit de is incorrect; say ce livre parle de or dans ce livre il s'agit de).

common_mistakes.correct: Dans ce film, il s'agit d'une histoire...
common_mistakes.explanation: Il s'agit de is exclusively impersonal.

grammar_rules.title: Conjugation of verbs ending in -eindre and -aindre
grammar_rules.summary: Singular drops 'd' and takes -s, -s, -t (je crains, il craint); plural stem has 'gn' (nous craignons, ils craignent).
grammar_rules.explanation: Verbs like peindre, craindre, plaindre, feindre, éteindre, atteindre conjugate: je peins, tu peins, il peint, nous peignons, vous peignez, ils peignent. Past participle ends in -t: peint, craint, plaint, éteint.

usage_notes: Invariable expression for presence and existence
Impersonal expression for the main theme or critical necessity

examples.english: In this book, it is about the French president.

examples.french: Il craint le pire pour les résultats.
